syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

chapters.title: Through the Eyes of Travellers: Perceptions of Society (c. tenth to seventeenth century)

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Al-Biruni's education, languages and how he came to Ghazni and to study India.
Explain the scope, language and distinctive chapter structure of the Kitab-ul-Hind.
Trace how the term 'Hindu' developed from a geographical to a religious meaning.
Outline Ibn Battuta's background, his career in Delhi and the route of his travels.
Explain how the Rihla was recorded and what it aimed to offer its readers.

topics.title: Francois Bernier: A Doctor with a Difference

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the Portuguese, French and other European travellers who wrote about India.
Evaluate Bernier's habit of comparing India with Europe and the spread of his writings.
Identify the barriers to understanding listed by Al-Biruni and the sources he relied on.
Analyse Al-Biruni's description of the varna system against social reality.
Explain why Al-Biruni rejected the notion of social pollution.

topics.title: Ibn Battuta and the Excitement of the Unfamiliar

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Ibn Battuta described unfamiliar things such as the coconut and the paan.
Interpret Ibn Battuta's picture of Indian cities, bazaars, agriculture and trade.
Describe the horse-post and foot-post and assess their efficiency.
Examine Bernier's argument about crown ownership of land and its supposed effects.
Trace how Bernier's ideas influenced Western theories of oriental despotism.
Evaluate the evidence that Mughal society and towns were more complex than Bernier claimed.
Analyse the evidence on slavery provided by Ibn Battuta.
Assess Bernier's account of sati and the wider evidence on women's work.

chapters.title: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions: Changes in Religious Beliefs and Devotional Texts (c. eighth to eighteenth century)

topics.title: A Mosaic of Religious Beliefs and Practices

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how local deities and goddess cults were integrated into the Puranic framework.
Describe the meaning of 'great' and 'little' traditions as used by Robert Redfield.
Distinguish Tantric, Vedic and Puranic practices and the tensions between them.

topics.title: Poems of Prayer: the Alvars and Nayanars of Tamil Nadu

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the Alvars and Nayanars and the compilations of their compositions.
Analyse the attitudes of Tamil bhaktas towards caste and the place of women devotees.
Explain why the Chola rulers patronised the Nayanar and Alvar traditions.

topics.title: The Virashaiva Tradition and Religious Ferment in North India

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the beliefs and practices of the Virashaivas or Lingayats led by Basavanna.
Explain the religious situation of north India, including the Naths, Jogis and Siddhas.

topics.title: New Strands in the Fabric: Islamic Traditions

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the category of zimmi and the flexible policies of rulers towards their subjects.
Describe how the universal features of Islam blended with local traditions.
Interpret the terms used in Sanskrit texts for migrant communities.

topics.title: The Growth of Sufism and the Chishtis in the Subcontinent

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the khanqah, silsila and the difference between ba-shari'a and be-shari'a sufis.
Explain Chishti practices such as ziyarat, sama' and the use of local languages.
Analyse the relationship between the Chishti sufis and the state.

topics.title: New Devotional Paths: Kabir, Baba Guru Nanak and Mirabai

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Kabir's ideas, the compilations of his verses and debates about his life.
Explain the teachings of Baba Guru Nanak and how his message was preserved.
Describe Mirabai's life and legacy as reconstructed from her bhajans.
Distinguish the genres of sufi texts such as malfuzat, maktubat and tazkiras.
Evaluate the challenges historians face in using sources on religious traditions.
Identify Colin Mackenzie's role in bringing the ruins of Hampi to light and his reasons for surveying the site.
Explain how oral traditions, inscriptions, photographs, travellers' accounts and literature were combined to rediscover Vijayanagara.

topics.title: Rayas, Nayakas and Sultans: Kings, Traders and the Course of the Empire

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the import of horses and overseas trade mattered to the rulers of Vijayanagara.
Describe the succession of ruling dynasties and the expansion of the empire under Krishnadeva Raya.
Analyse the relations between the rayas and the Deccan Sultans and the causes of the defeat of 1565.
Describe who the nayakas were and how they related to the kings of Vijayanagara.
Explain the working of the amara-nayaka system and its role in the collapse of the imperial structure.
Explain how the water requirements of Vijayanagara were met through tanks, canals and reservoirs.
Describe the fortifications and roads of the city and explain why agricultural tracts were enclosed.
Interpret archaeological and textual evidence about the urban core and the lives of its residents.
Describe the temples and palace complexes of the royal centre and the materials used to build them.
Explain the rituals associated with the mahanavami dibba and evaluate the evidence about its use.
Identify the Lotus Mahal and the Hazara Rama temple and what is known about their use.
Explain how sacred traditions and temple patronage shaped the choice of the capital and royal claims to authority.
Describe the gopurams, mandapas and other features of the Virupaksha and Vitthala temples.

topics.title: Plotting Palaces, Temples and Bazaars; Questions in Search of Answers

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Hampi was preserved, surveyed and mapped in the twentieth century.
Evaluate what surviving buildings can and cannot tell historians about Vijayanagara.

chapters.title: Peasants, Zamindars and the State: Agrarian Society and the Mughal Empire

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the main sources for Mughal agrarian history and explain why the Ain gives a view from the top.
Distinguish between khud-kashta and pahi-kashta peasants and the reasons people became pahi-kashta.
Explain the size of peasant holdings and the principle of individual ownership of land.

topics.title: Irrigation, technology and an abundance of crops

concepts.learning_objective: Relate rainfall and the kharif and rabi cycles to the staple crops grown in Mughal India.
Describe the irrigation devices and agricultural tools used by peasants.
Explain jins-i kamil and the spread of new crops such as tobacco and maize.
Explain how caste shaped the position of different groups in rural society.
Describe the functions of village panchayats, jati panchayats and headmen, and peasant resistance.
Explain how village artisans were paid and evaluate the idea of the village as a little republic.
Describe the roles of women in agricultural and artisanal production.
Explain social customs such as bride-price and remarriage in peasant communities.
Evaluate the property rights of women and their petitions to the panchayat.
Describe the extent of forests and the livelihood of forest dwellers termed jangli.
Analyse how the state, commerce and culture made inroads into forest areas.
Explain how tribal chiefs became zamindars or kings and built armies.
Identify the sources of the zamindars' power, including milkiyat lands and military resources.
Explain how zamindaris originated and were consolidated, and their role in colonising land.
Evaluate the element of reciprocity and patronage in zamindar-peasant relations.

topics.title: Land revenue system and the flow of silver

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the stages of assessment (jama) and collection (hasil) and the methods of collection in kind.
Classify lands under Akbar and calculate the revenue demand from the medium produce.
Explain how the flow of silver into India affected currency and revenue collection.

topics.title: The Ain-i Akbari of Abu'l Fazl Allami

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the purpose and the organisation of the Ain into its five daftars.
Evaluate the strengths and limitations of the Ain as a historical source.
